bug_semantics: The affected SDK methods insert caller-influenced identifiers directly into URL path template literals while attaching the merchant's bearer token. Slash or dot-dot content can be normalized by the WHATWG URL parser into a different API path, and a question mark can become attacker-chosen query syntax, so an application that passes an untrusted identifier without its own ownership check can make credentialed requests outside the intended resource. The affected families are payment get/capture/cancel, paymentRefund create/total/list/get, advancedPayment get/capture/cancel/update/updateReleaseDate, and disbursementRefund create/createAll/listAll.
flaw_origin: The smallest first mainline change among the advisory's affected methods is 7d83325f4760a079a0d3f3f69001c07a8d380657 ('payment refund client'). It created the payment-refund create/get/list implementations and directly interpolated payment_id (and refund_id for get) into /v1/payments/... paths. Later additions extended the same pre-existing flaw: payment capture in 6008b53014be88d6757e89ec42688ce7d8906fe0, cancel in 0fdb24947c5f0e211d49e6d169f53b461c1dc2c3, get in 203000cd6d49d416ff8a50ca4cae290da4b92b13, refund total in 3c58ca7b51d8917681b56d5ae17265d21c047d4c, and the advancedPayment/disbursementRefund clients in adcaceaa233f5c7cb67d4723d6b7ca0cfdd25e2b. Renames and later refactors were rejected as origins.
ai_marker: Absent. `git cat-file commit 7d83325f4760a079a0d3f3f69001c07a8d380657` shows author and committer Bruna Campos <bruna.camposf@mercadolivre.com> and the message `payment refund client`; there is no bot identity, Co-Authored-By AI identity, Generated-with trailer, or other AI marker in that BIC commit object.
evidence: GitHub advisory GHSA-8vxq-h2gr-x277 (published 2026-08-24) describes the raw path interpolation attack and lists affected and patched versions as Unknown; its description explicitly says PR #451 applied encodePathParam to roughly 29 other clients while leaving the named payment, paymentRefund, advancedPayment, and disbursementRefund methods unchanged.

Run `git show --format=fuller --patch 7d83325f4760a079a0d3f3f69001c07a8d380657` in the validated clone. The commit creates src/clients/paymentsRefunds/create/index.ts with `/v1/payments/${payment_id}/refunds`, get/index.ts with `/v1/payments/${payment_id}/refunds/${refund_id}`, and getList/index.ts with `/v1/payments/${payment_id}/refunds/`; every request carries Authorization: Bearer ${config.accessToken}.

Run `git log --date=iso-strict --pretty=fuller -L 20,23:src/clients/paymentRefund/create/index.ts master`. The current vulnerable create path follows through naming/type-only changes to 7d83325f4760a079a0d3f3f69001c07a8d380657; the BIC creates the function and raw interpolation from /dev/null. Cross-check with `git log --all --reverse -S'/v1/payments/' -- src`: 7d83325f4760a079a0d3f3f69001c07a8d380657 is the first commit that adds a dynamic /v1/payments/ path in an advisory-listed method (the earlier 7ee497d0490d62e69d57da6c3a57edd2f94f8839 hit only changes the constant payment-search path).

Direct-parent check: `git ls-tree -r --name-only 6ad06e6670735c3881c8925ba25000593eddbb83 -- src/clients/paymentsRefunds src/clients/refunds` has no paymentsRefunds implementation and shows only placeholder refunds files; `git show 6ad06e6670735c3881c8925ba25000593eddbb83:src/clients/refunds/create/index.ts` (and get/index.ts and getList/index.ts) produces empty content. Thus the parent lacks the vulnerable request construction.

Lifecycle expansion is reproducible with `git log --all --reverse -S'/v1/payments/' -- src` and `git show` on 6008b53014be88d6757e89ec42688ce7d8906fe0, 0fdb24947c5f0e211d49e6d169f53b461c1dc2c3, 203000cd6d49d416ff8a50ca4cae290da4b92b13, 3c58ca7b51d8917681b56d5ae17265d21c047d4c, and adcaceaa233f5c7cb67d4723d6b7ca0cfdd25e2b. The last commit creates all affected advancedPayment and disbursementRefund path builders on mainline; the similarly named 2025 AI feature commits exist only on origin/feature/advanced_payment_IA and are not ancestors of master, so they are not the shipped BIC.

Version boundary: `git tag --contains 7d83325f4760a079a0d3f3f69001c07a8d380657 --sort=version:refname` starts at 2.0.0, whose tag commit is cb7eb3603b4acf13aa8dc65ab1741df1542f2d77. The advancedPayment/disbursementRefund expansion adcaceaa233f5c7cb67d4723d6b7ca0cfdd25e2b first appears in release 3.1.0.

PR #451 is only a partial remediation: merge 068e5d8e4ba0518872533c58cca8cd9a2a8a6d55 contains direct commit 66daf6b95fc7768741ee8460d74dbda95e8cd586, which creates src/utils/path.ts and applies encodePathParam elsewhere. `git diff --stat 66daf6b95fc7768741ee8460d74dbda95e8cd586^ 66daf6b95fc7768741ee8460d74dbda95e8cd586 -- src/clients/payment src/clients/paymentRefund src/clients/advancedPayment src/clients/disbursementRefund` is empty. `git tag --contains 068e5d8e4ba0518872533c58cca8cd9a2a8a6d55` starts at 3.2.1, but it is not a closing fix for this advisory.

Unpatched boundary: master and tag 3.6.0 both resolve to c8da864cd370d179ad10e182e4793510d6d03bfe. `git show 3.6.0:src/clients/paymentRefund/create/index.ts` still contains `/v1/payments/${payment_id}/refunds`, and `git show 3.6.0:src/clients/advancedPayment/get/index.ts` still contains `/v1/advanced_payments/${id}` without encodePathParam. Therefore no closing fix commit or patched release exists in the available public history through 3.6.0.

BIC-only AI check: `git cat-file commit 7d83325f4760a079a0d3f3f69001c07a8d380657` prints one human author/committer, one parent, and only the subject `payment refund client`; no AI trailer or bot identity is present. Later branch commits mentioning IA/AI and later AI-authored work are excluded by the protocol because they are not the BIC commit object.
reasoning: The advisory covers one repeated failure to encode an identifier as one URL segment. History shows the first affected implementation was not the later AI-named advanced-payment work but the payment-refund client added in 2023. Its direct parent had empty refund placeholders, while the BIC added executable credentialed requests with raw interpolations; subsequent renames and type refactors preserve those exact vulnerable lines, and later endpoint commits only broaden the attack surface. The first containing release is 2.0.0. PR #451 introduced the intended encoder in 3.2.1 but did not touch any advisory-listed family, and 3.6.0 remains vulnerable, so fix SHAs are null rather than incorrectly treating that partial hardening as closure. The BIC commit object has a human identity and no AI marker, making NOT_AI the supported BIC-only verdict even though unrelated or non-mainline later commits mention AI.
remaining_gap: Unpatched in the public repository as of master/tag 3.6.0 (c8da864cd370d179ad10e182e4793510d6d03bfe); consequently there is no closing fix SHA, direct fix SHA, or patched-version boundary to record.
